category: Physics interfaces IV: heat transfer features
description: Heat Transfer Module interfaces and nodes beyond the basic ones: porous media, bioheat, radiation in participating media, moisture transport, lumped thermal systems, heat transfer in shells, thin layers, convective heat-flux correlations, phase change, thermal contact, line/point/boundary sources, outflow/open/symmetry boundaries, isothermal domains, surface-to-surface radiation surfaces, conjugate heat transfer and thermoelectric couplings. API: model.component("comp1").physics().create(tag, type, "geom1") and physics(tag).create(ftag, type, dim).

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Porous Media (ht)
tools.description: Version of the Heat Transfer interface whose default domain node is Porous Medium: it solves one temperature for fluid and solid phases with effective (volume-averaged) properties computed from porosity and the phase properties, and can switch to a local thermal non-equilibrium (two-temperature) model. Used for packed beds, insulation, soils, catalytic reactors and heat exchangers with porous inserts, usually coupled to Darcy/Brinkman flow.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Porous Media > Heat Transfer in Porous Media (ht); API: physics().create("ht", "PorousMediaHeatTransfer", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Medium > Fluid / Porous Matrix subnodes
parameters.description: Fluid velocity field (from a flow interface), fluid and solid properties, porosity.

parameters.name: Effective conductivity
parameters.description: Volume average, reciprocal average, power law, or user defined.

parameters.name: Thermal dispersion
parameters.description: Optional velocity-dependent dispersion tensor.

parameters.name: Local thermal nonequilibrium
parameters.description: Two temperatures with interstitial heat transfer coefficient.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module (or Subsurface Flow / Porous Media Flow Module). Porous Medium can also be added as a domain node to any Heat Transfer interface. The Local Thermal Nonequilibrium multiphysics interface couples two separate Heat Transfer interfaces instead.

tools.name: Bioheat Transfer (ht)
tools.description: Heat Transfer interface whose default domain node is Biological Tissue with the Bioheat subnode implementing the Pennes equation: blood perfusion (rate, blood density, heat capacity and arterial temperature) and metabolic heat source, plus optional tissue damage integrals (Arrhenius or temperature-threshold). Used for hyperthermia, RF/microwave ablation, cryosurgery, laser treatment and thermal comfort models.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Bioheat Transfer (ht); API: physics().create("ht", "BioHeat", "geom1")

parameters.name: Biological Tissue > Bioheat subnode
parameters.description: Arterial blood temperature Tb, blood specific heat Cb, perfusion rate omega_b, metabolic heat source Qmet.

parameters.name: Thermal Damage subnode
parameters.description: Damage model (energy absorption/Arrhenius or temperature threshold) giving ht.theta_d fraction of necrotic tissue.

parameters.name: Include damage in material properties
parameters.description: Switch conductivity/heat capacity to damaged-tissue values.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module. Combine with Electric Currents or Electromagnetic Waves through Electromagnetic Heating for ablation; the Bioheat Transfer material library entries provide tissue properties.

tools.name: Radiation in Participating Media (rpm)
tools.description: Solves the radiative transfer equation in semi-transparent absorbing, emitting and scattering media (glass melts, combustion gases, tissue, atmospheres) with the discrete ordinates method (Sn quadrature) or the P1 approximation, and in 6.x also the discrete transfer / DOM with several quadrature sets. Coupled to Heat Transfer through the Heat Transfer with Radiation in Participating Media multiphysics interface, it supplies the radiative heat source and takes the temperature for emission.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Radiation in Participating Media (rpm); API: physics().create("rpm", "ParticipatingMediaRadiation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Radiation discretization method
parameters.description: Discrete ordinates (S2, S4, S6, S8) or P1 approximation.

parameters.name: Participating Medium node
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient, scattering coefficient and phase function (isotropic, linear anisotropic, Henyey-Greenstein), refractive index.

parameters.name: Opaque Surface / Semitransparent Surface
parameters.description: Boundary emissivity and diffuse/specular reflection.

parameters.name: Incident Intensity
parameters.description: External radiation entering through a boundary.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module. DOM adds one DOF per direction (S4 = 24 directions in 3D), so memory grows quickly; P1 is cheap but only valid for optically thick media. Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media (rasm) is the variant without emission, and Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media (rbam) handles collimated beams (Beer-Lambert).

tools.name: Moisture Transport in Air (mt)
tools.description: Solves for the relative humidity (or vapor concentration) in air by convection-diffusion of water vapor, including evaporation/condensation at surfaces and coupling to heat transfer through latent heat. Moisture Transport in Building Materials and in Porous Media are companion interfaces for hygroscopic solids; the Heat and Moisture and Moisture Flow multiphysics interfaces couple them with Heat Transfer and fluid flow for HVAC, food drying, electronics condensation and building physics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Moisture Transport > Moisture Transport in Air (mt); API: physics().create("mt", "MoistureTransportInAir", "geom1")

parameters.name: Moist Air domain node
parameters.description: Velocity field and diffusion coefficient of vapor in air.

parameters.name: Moisture Content / Moisture Flux / Wet Surface / Moist Surface
parameters.description: Boundary conditions (prescribed humidity, flux, evaporating film).

parameters.name: Heat and Moisture multiphysics
parameters.description: Couples latent heat and temperature-dependent saturation.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module. Use the Moist Air fluid type in Heat Transfer in Fluids so that properties follow humidity. Condensation on cold walls uses the Wet Surface / Moist Surface features with the Heat Transfer coupling.

tools.name: Lumped Thermal System (lts)
tools.description: Zero-dimensional network interface (analogous to Electrical Circuit) of thermal resistances, capacitances, heat sources, radiative links, thermal mass and external terminals, solved together with FEM heat transfer through External Terminal nodes on boundaries. It models the rest of a system - heat sinks, housings, ambient stages - cheaply while the component of interest is meshed, and is common in electronics cooling and spacecraft thermal models.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Lumped Thermal System (lts); API: physics().create("lts", "LumpedThermalSystem", "geom1"); lts.create("R1", "ConductiveThermalResistor", -1)

parameters.name: Nodes
parameters.description: Integer node names; connections given as node pairs.

parameters.name: Element types
parameters.description: Conductive Thermal Resistor, Convective Thermal Resistor, Radiative Thermal Resistor, Thermal Capacitor, Thermal Mass, Heat Rate Source, Temperature, Thermal Pipe, Heat Pipe, Subsystem.

parameters.name: External Terminal
parameters.description: Connects a lumped node to a boundary of a Heat Transfer interface (with the Lumped Thermal Connector multiphysics).

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module (5.6+). Node temperatures are lts.T_1 etc.; heat rates lts.R1_P. Radiative resistors need view factors supplied by the user.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Shells (htlsh)
tools.description: Boundary interface solving heat conduction (and convection/radiation to the surroundings) in thin structures represented by surfaces - sheet metal, PCBs, composite laminates, tank walls - with a given thickness and, for layered materials, a through-thickness discretisation so temperature gradients across the laminate are captured. Couples to 3D Heat Transfer domains through shared boundaries and to Layered Shell / Shell mechanics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Thin Structures > Heat Transfer in Shells (htlsh); API: physics().create("htlsh", "HeatTransferInShellsLM", "geom1")

parameters.name: Shell model
parameters.description: Layered shell (from a Layered Material) or nonlayered shell with thickness Lth.

parameters.name: Solid / Fluid / Porous Medium (shell) nodes
parameters.description: Material of the shell layer(s).

parameters.name: Heat Flux / Temperature / Heat Source (edge and surface)
parameters.description: Conditions on the shell surfaces and edges.

parameters.name: Layered Material Slice plots
parameters.description: Results through the thickness.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module (the Composite Materials Module adds layered features). Thin Layer / Thin Film / Fracture nodes inside a 3D Heat Transfer interface are the alternative when the thin structure sits between meshed domains.

tools.name: Thin Layer
tools.description: Boundary node in Heat Transfer in Solids that represents a thin solid layer (coating, glue line, oxide, insulation foil, PCB laminate) on an interior or exterior boundary without meshing it: Thermally thin (resistive, in-plane conduction neglected or included), Thermally thick (through-thickness gradient with a 1D discretisation) or General (layered material with in-plane and through-thickness conduction). It replaces the older Thin Layer/Thermally Thin Layer features and the Thermal Contact node for simple gaps.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer in Solids > Thin Structures > Thin Layer (tl1); API: physics("ht").create("tl1", "SolidLayeredShell", 2)

parameters.name: Layer type
parameters.description: Thermally thin approximation | Thermally thick approximation | General.

parameters.name: Lth / thermal conductivity
parameters.description: Thickness and properties (from material or Layered Material).

parameters.name: Heat Source / Temperature subnodes
parameters.description: Sources and conditions inside the layer.

tools.notes: Thin Film (fluid layer) and Fracture (porous layer) are the fluid/porous analogues. A resistive layer on an interior boundary creates a temperature jump; results on the two sides are ht.Td and ht.Tu (down/up).

tools.name: Convective Heat Flux (heat transfer coefficient correlations)
tools.description: Heat Flux boundary node with Flux type 'Convective heat flux' q = h (Text - T), where h is either user defined or taken from a library of built-in Nusselt correlations: external natural convection (vertical/inclined plate, horizontal plate up/down, cylinder, sphere), internal natural convection (parallel plates, channels), external forced convection (plate, cylinder, sphere) and internal forced convection (isothermal tube) - each parametrised by geometry length, external fluid (air by default, from the material library), pressure, velocity and temperature.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Heat Flux (hf1) > Flux type: Convective heat flux > Heat transfer coefficient: External natural convection...; API: physics("ht").feature("hf1").set("HeatFluxType", "ConvectiveHeatFlux"); set("HeatTransferCoefficientType", "ExtNaturalConvection")

parameters.name: HeatFluxType
parameters.description: GeneralInwardHeatFlux | ConvectiveHeatFlux | HeatRate.

parameters.name: HeatTransferCoefficientType
parameters.description: UserDefined | ExtNaturalConvection | IntNaturalConvection | ExtForcedConvection | IntForcedConvection.

parameters.name: Geometry option and length
parameters.description: e.g. VerticalWall with wall height L, HorizontalPlateUpside with characteristic length, Cylinder with diameter.

parameters.name: Text, pA, Uext
parameters.description: External temperature, absolute pressure and (forced) velocity.

tools.notes: The correlations are in the core product; the external fluid properties come from the built-in Air/Water definitions. The 'Heat Flux' entry in the first physics chunk covers the general inward flux form.

tools.name: Phase Change Material
tools.description: Subnode of Solid / Fluid / Porous Medium domain nodes in Heat Transfer that implements melting/solidification with the apparent heat capacity method: between phases the latent heat is spread over a transition interval dT around the phase-change temperature, and the properties switch smoothly from phase 1 to phase 2 (up to several transitions). Used for PCM heat storage, casting, ice formation, welding pools and food freezing.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Solid 1 > Phase Change Material (pcm1); API: physics("ht").feature("solid1").create("pcm1", "PhaseChangeMaterial", 3)

parameters.name: Number of phase transitions
parameters.description: 1 or more.

parameters.name: Tpc1_2 / dT1_2 / L1_2
parameters.description: Phase change temperature, transition interval and latent heat.

parameters.name: Phase 1 / Phase 2 materials
parameters.description: Separate materials (or user values) for each phase.

tools.notes: Core product feature. The time step and mesh must resolve the transition interval (a few elements across the mushy zone); the phase indicator ht.theta and the liquid fraction are available for plots. For Stefan problems with a sharp front use Deformed Geometry with a Phase Change Interface node (Heat Transfer Module).

tools.name: Thermal Contact
tools.description: Pair or interior-boundary feature modelling the imperfect thermal contact between two solids: a contact conductance from the Cooper-Mikic-Yovanovich or Mikic elastic correlations (surface roughness, hardness, contact pressure) or a user value, plus gap gas conductance and radiation across the gap. Used for bolted joints, heat sink-to-chip interfaces, pressed contacts and thermal interface materials.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Pairs > Thermal Contact (tc1) or Thin Structures > Thermal Contact on interior boundaries; API: physics("ht").create("tc1", "ThermalContact", 2)

parameters.name: Contact conductance
parameters.description: Cooper-Mikic-Yovanovich | Mikic elastic | User defined h_c.

parameters.name: Contact pressure / roughness / hardness
parameters.description: Inputs for the correlations; pressure can come from a structural contact (solid.cnt1.Tn).

parameters.name: Gap conductance / radiation
parameters.description: Gas thermal conductivity and emissivities in the gap.

tools.notes: Core product feature (contact correlations from the Heat Transfer Module). On an assembly it is a pair feature; on a union it can be applied on interior boundaries directly (6.x).

tools.name: Outflow (heat transfer)
tools.description: Boundary condition for Heat Transfer in Fluids stating that heat leaves the domain only by convection, -n.(k grad T) = 0, i.e. the conductive flux is zero and the temperature is carried out by the flow. It is the correct condition at fluid outlets and is applied automatically by the Nonisothermal Flow interface on Outlet boundaries.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer in Fluids > Outflow (ofl1); API: physics("ht").create("ofl1", "ConvectiveOutflow", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Outlet boundaries of the fluid.

tools.notes: Do not use Outflow where the flow reverses; use Open Boundary there. Inflow (6.x) is the matching inlet condition specifying upstream temperature and pressure rather than a Dirichlet temperature.

tools.name: Open Boundary (heat transfer)
tools.description: Boundary condition for fluid domains where flow may enter or leave: where the flow enters the domain the temperature is set to the exterior temperature T0 (inflow), where it leaves the Outflow condition applies. Needed on far-field boundaries of natural-convection models and on open ends of ducts with recirculation.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer in Fluids > Open Boundary (ob1); API: physics("ht").create("ob1", "OpenBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: T0
parameters.description: Exterior (upstream) temperature.

tools.notes: Pair it with the Open Boundary node of the flow interface on the same boundaries.

tools.name: Symmetry (heat transfer)
tools.description: Boundary condition -n.q = 0 (no heat flux across the boundary), identical in effect to Thermal Insulation but semantically marking a symmetry plane; the default exterior condition already is Thermal Insulation, so this node is mostly for clarity and for surface-to-surface radiation models where symmetry must be declared explicitly (Symmetry for Surface-to-Surface Radiation).
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Symmetry (sym1); API: physics("ht").create("sym1", "Symmetry", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Symmetry planes.

tools.notes: In the Surface-to-Surface Radiation interface, symmetry planes must be declared in the Symmetry for Surface-to-Surface Radiation node so view factors account for the mirrored geometry.

tools.name: Initial Values (heat transfer)
tools.description: Default domain node (init1) setting the initial temperature for time-dependent studies and the initial guess for nonlinear stationary solves; additional Initial Values nodes give different regions different starting temperatures. The value can be an expression, a function of position, or the solution of another study through the study's Values of Dependent Variables settings.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Initial Values (init1 default); API: physics("ht").feature("init1").set("Tinit", "293.15[K]")

parameters.name: Tinit
parameters.description: Initial temperature (default the Default Model Inputs temperature, 293.15 K).

tools.notes: Every physics interface has an Initial Values node with the same role (solid: u, v, w and velocities; spf: u, p; es: V...). For a smooth transient start, make initial values consistent with the boundary conditions at t = 0 or use a ramp.

tools.name: Line Heat Source
tools.description: Edge (3D) or point (2D) source that deposits a heat rate per unit length Pl (or a total power over the edge) - a thin heating wire, a laser line, a buried cable or a heat pipe modelled as an edge - without meshing the wire's cross-section. Line Heat Source on Axis exists for 2D axisymmetric models, and Line Heat Source (Thin Rod) combines it with rod conduction.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Edges > Line Heat Source (lhs1); API: physics("ht").create("lhs1", "LineHeatSource", 1)

parameters.name: Pl
parameters.description: Heat rate per unit length (W/m), or Ql total power with 'Total power' option.

parameters.name: Line source radius
parameters.description: Optional radius to regularise the singular temperature field.

tools.notes: The temperature at a line source is singular (logarithmic); evaluate at a small distance or specify the source radius. Point Heat Source and Boundary Heat Source are the 0D and 2D analogues.

tools.name: Point Heat Source
tools.description: Point feature adding a total heat rate Pp (W) at a geometry vertex, for small components (a chip, an LED, a thermocouple junction) whose size is negligible compared with the model; the Point Heat Source on Axis variant serves 2D axisymmetric geometries. Because a point source gives a 1/r temperature singularity in 3D, use it only when the temperature at the source itself is not needed, or set the point source radius.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Points > Point Heat Source (phs1); API: physics("ht").create("phs1", "PointHeatSource", 0)

parameters.name: Pp
parameters.description: Heat rate (W); can be an expression of time or temperature.

parameters.name: Point source radius
parameters.description: Regularisation radius (6.x).

tools.notes: For a realistic chip use a small domain with a Heat Source (total power option) or a Boundary Heat Source over the footprint instead.

tools.name: Boundary Heat Source
tools.description: Boundary node adding a heat flux density Qb (W/m^2) or a total boundary power Pb distributed over the selection, on interior or exterior boundaries - thin-film heaters, absorbed laser/solar power on a surface, frictional heating, or a source computed by another physics (e.g. ec.Qsh from a thin conducting layer). Interior boundary sources heat both adjacent domains.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Boundaries > Boundary Heat Source (bhs1); API: physics("ht").create("bhs1", "BoundaryHeatSource", 2)

parameters.name: Qb / Pb
parameters.description: Heat flux density, or total power with the 'Overall heat transfer rate' option (Pb_tot).

parameters.name: Source position
parameters.description: Layer position for layered/thin structures (6.x).

tools.notes: Heat Flux (exterior) and Boundary Heat Source (interior or exterior) coincide on exterior boundaries for a general inward flux; prefer Heat Flux when a convective/ambient part is involved. Deposited Beam Power gives a Gaussian/top-hat beam footprint directly.

tools.name: Diffuse Surface
tools.description: Boundary node of the Surface-to-Surface Radiation interface (rad) that marks a surface as an opaque, diffusely emitting and reflecting (grey or spectrally banded) participant in the radiosity/view-factor computation, with emissivity from the material, an ambient temperature for openings and a radiation direction (upside/downside/both). Every surface that exchanges radiation with others must carry this node (or Diffuse Mirror / Opaque Surface / Semitransparent Surface variants); Surface-to-Ambient Radiation in Heat Transfer is the cheap alternative when only exchange with a far ambient matters.
tools.usage: Physics > Surface-to-Surface Radiation > Diffuse Surface (ds1 default); API: physics("rad").create("ds2", "DiffuseSurface", 2)

parameters.name: epsilon_rad
parameters.description: Surface emissivity (per spectral band when multiple bands are used).

parameters.name: Radiation direction
parameters.description: Opacity controlled | Positive normal | Negative normal | Both sides.

parameters.name: Ambient temperature Tamb
parameters.description: For radiation leaving through openings (view factor to ambient).

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module. View factors are computed with hemicube (default) or direct area integration or ray shooting (6.x); the Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation multiphysics node links rad to ht. Symmetry planes must be declared in the rad interface.

tools.name: Isothermal Domain
tools.description: Domain node that replaces the temperature field in a selection by a single lumped temperature (a well-mixed fluid tank, a highly conductive block, a component with negligible internal gradients) governed by an energy balance with its surroundings; the Isothermal Domain Interface boundary node sets the exchange (thermal insulation, continuity, ventilation, convective heat flux, thermal contact). It reduces cost and removes stiff conduction from the system.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Isothermal Domain (id1) (enable 'Isothermal domain' in the interface's Physical Model section); API: physics("ht").prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("IsothermalDomain", true); physics("ht").create("id1", "IsothermalDomain", 3)

parameters.name: Mass / heat capacity source
parameters.description: From density and volume or user defined.

parameters.name: Isothermal Domain Interface subnode
parameters.description: Interface type: Thermal insulation | Continuity | Ventilation | Convective heat flux | Thermal contact.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module. The domain temperature is a global variable (ht.id1.T) usable in probes and other physics.

tools.name: Thermal Insulation
tools.description: Default exterior boundary condition of every Heat Transfer interface: -n.q = 0, no conductive heat flux across the boundary (adiabatic wall, symmetry plane, or an interface to an unmodelled perfect insulator). Extra Thermal Insulation nodes are used to override other conditions on subsets of boundaries.
tools.usage: Physics > Heat Transfer > Thermal Insulation (ins1 default); API: physics("ht").create("ins2", "ThermalInsulation", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries with zero normal flux.

tools.notes: Later nodes in the tree override earlier ones on shared boundaries, so an explicit Thermal Insulation after a Heat Flux node switches those boundaries back to adiabatic.

tools.name: Conjugate Heat Transfer (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface (Heat Transfer > Conjugate Heat Transfer > Laminar Flow / Turbulent Flow variants) that adds a Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids interface, a Laminar or Turbulent Flow interface and the Nonisothermal Flow multiphysics coupling (nitf1), which passes the velocity field to the energy equation, the temperature-dependent density/viscosity back to the flow, and handles viscous dissipation, pressure work and turbulent thermal conductivity with wall functions. It is the standard starting point for heat sinks, heat exchangers, electronics cooling and natural convection in enclosures.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Conjugate Heat Transfer > Laminar Flow; API: physics().create("ht", "HeatTransferInSolidsAndFluids", "geom1"); physics().create("spf", "LaminarFlow", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("nitf1", "NonIsothermalFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Fluid / Solid domain nodes (ht)
parameters.description: Assigned so that the flow domains are Fluid and the rest Solid.

parameters.name: Nonisothermal Flow coupling settings
parameters.description: Include viscous dissipation, pressure work, gravity/Boussinesq (via spf gravity), turbulent Prandtl number, wall treatment.

parameters.name: Compressibility (spf)
parameters.description: Weakly compressible is the default for natural convection with temperature-dependent density.

tools.notes: Core product for laminar flow; turbulent variants need the CFD or Heat Transfer Module. Natural convection: enable Gravity in spf and use the Stationary study with pseudo time stepping; the Nonisothermal Flow interface (Fluid Flow branch) is identical but lists the flow first.

tools.name: Thermoelectric Effect (multiphysics)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling between Electric Currents and Heat Transfer in Solids that adds the Seebeck, Peltier and Thomson effects: the current density gains the term -sigma S grad T and the heat flux the Peltier term S T J, on top of Joule heating. Used for thermoelectric coolers and generators, thermocouples and Peltier-driven MEMS; the Thermoelectric Effect predefined interface adds ec, ht and the coupling.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Electromagnetic Heating > Thermoelectric Effect; API: multiphysics().create("tee1", "ThermoelectricEffect", 3)

parameters.name: Seebeck coefficient S
parameters.description: From material (thermoelectric material library) or user; sign gives n/p type.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: ec and ht tags.

parameters.name: Boundary Thermoelectric Effect
parameters.description: Companion coupling for thin shells (ecs + htlsh).

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module or AC/DC Module. Electromagnetic Heating (Joule heating) must also be present for a complete energy balance; the predefined interface adds both.
